datasets.title: Nigeria - FEWSNET IPC Acute Food Security Classifications over Time: A Public Health and Food Security Synthesis Report with Corresponding Data
datasets.description: This report explores food insecurity in Nigeria in the context of urbanization and demographic change. A comparison of changing acute food security measures (IPC) from January and February 2010-2018 accompanies the report. The authors, Jordan Burnett, Leah Nadel, Victoria Santiago, and Arline Tarazona, completed their research in partial fulfillment of Public Health coursework in Medical Geography, for Spring 2018, at Drew University. Dr. Lisa Jordan edited the report and supplemented their work with additional spatial data.. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/nigeria-fewsnet-ipc-acute-food-security-classifications-over-time-2009-2018]
datasets.details: Lisa Jordan assembled the Nigeria data set, but the original source is FEWS NET. Please acknowledge FEWS.net for present and historical data using the IPC system to classify acute food security. Consult FEWS NET or IPCInfo for documentation on appropriate display of IPC classes.

lineage.description: FEWS.net IPC acute food security classification shapefiles for Nigeria (2010-2018) were obtained and analyzed by Drew University researchers to characterize temporal trends in food insecurity phases across administrative regions. The dataset synthesizes historical IPC classifications to document changing patterns of food security status over an 8-year period in the context of urbanization and demographic change.

sources.name: FEWS.net (Famine Early Warning Systems Network)
sources.description: Distributes historical and current shapefiles characterizing regions by IPC acute food security classification phases (1=Minimal to 5=Famine). Data aggregated and analyzed by Drew University researchers for temporal comparison 2010-2018.

resources.title: fewsnet_nga.zip
resources.description: FEWS NET IPC Acute Food Security Classification for Nigeria (2009-2018) stored as shapefiles, by year and month (3-4 times annually). Attributes(s): CS: Current Status (IPC Value 1-5, or 99 for missing data or not monitored) HA0: the value 1 indicates that the situation would be worse on the IPC scale if not for humanitarian aid, 0 otherwise

resources.description: In the 'Food Security and Public Health Synthesis Report - Case Study of Nigeria,' Jordan Burnett, Leah Nadel, Victoria Santiago, and Arline Tarazona explore how urbanization, demography, and conflict are contributing factors in acute food insecurity.
